_comment: Dungeons and raids of WoW Forever for the addon's dungeon planner, kept by hand. tools/build_dungeons.py turns this file into Amisia/Data/DungeonData.lua. Facts only: names, level ranges, group sizes, bosses known so far, opening dates and instance ids; never a loot table, a drop chance or a list taken from a fan site. Each entry names its source in "src" (see "sources"); a field whose facts come from elsewhere names that in "<field>_src" (bosses_src, aliases_src, inst_src). Fields: key (short id), name (English, as the item data names it), kind (party or raid), min/max (level range; null while unknown), size (players; null while unknown), inst (instance id; null until the client reports it through the drop records), area (area id), from (opening date), bosses (names known so far), aliases (other spellings the item data and quests use), part (the client's name of an instance that hosts several dungeons; the planner then places an NPC of that instance by the dungeon whose data lists it), att_wing (AllTheThings' header of the bosses of such a dungeon), order and enc (the bosses in the game's order with their encounter ids, only where the client tables have none and a source gives the order; else the build takes the client's or AllTheThings'), boss_alias (a boss name of the order -> the name AllTheThings lists that boss under; the NPC id always comes from AllTheThings).

sources.public: Public facts on WoW Forever's new dungeons and raids as the user gave them on 2026-10-05: names, level ranges, raid sizes and the raid opening on 2026-12-09. Instance ids are left empty (Onyxia's Lair: see zones); the client reports them through the drop records.
sources.repo: Classic dungeons as the repo's own data names them: the dungeon sources and dungeon quests of Amisia/Data/GearData.lua (tools/build_gear.py) and the entrances of Amisia/Data/MapData.lua (tools/build_map.py). Their level ranges and sizes stay empty here: the client's LFGDungeons table (wago CSV, downloaded by hand) gives no range or size, only, through ContentTuning, the one level the client tunes a dungeon to, the low end of its range (equal to the public minimum of the four new dungeons that have both). tools/build_dungeons.py --wago keeps that level and the instance id (AreaTable) in tools/forever_dungeons_client.json; the addon takes the level as the low end and the required levels of the dungeon's items for the high end, and marks the range as an estimate. The item data's plain "Blackrock Spire" records (War Master Voone, Goraluk Anvilcrack) belong to Lower Blackrock Spire, where those bosses stand; both halves are parts of the one instance the client calls "Blackrock Spire".
sources.repo:GearData: Boss names and spellings as the dungeon sources of Amisia/Data/GearData.lua (tools/build_gear.py) give them: the named bosses of the dungeon's D records (its captains and other named mobs left out). Checked against that file by tools/tests/test_build_dungeons.py.
sources.zones: Onyxia's Lair: instance id 249 and area id 2159 from tools/forever_zones.json.
sources.att: The instance list of AllTheThings' hand-kept Forever data (MIT, read by tools/att_data.py; its Classic folders for the Classic dungeons): the instance's name as that data writes it. Used where the repo's own data does not name the dungeon (yet), e.g. while the item scan has not seen its loot. att_wing: the name of the instance's own header (createHeader) under which that data lists the bosses of one dungeon of an instance that hosts several (Blackrock Spire: "Hordemar City (Lower)", "Dragonspire Hall (Upper)").
sources.att:alias: boss_alias: a boss name of the client's encounter table (DungeonEncounter) -> the NPC name under which AllTheThings (MIT) lists that boss in the same instance, checked by hand on 2026-11-10 (D-100): Geilhast is the client's spelling of Gelihast (Blackfathom Deeps); The Lost Dwarves (Uldaman) is the group of Baelog, Eric "The Swift" and Olaf, Baelog stands for it (ATT lists him first, he gives the quest chain); The Vault (Blackrock Depths) is the fight of Watchman Doomgrip (ATT: he spawns once all twelve Relic Coffers of the vault are open); Ezra Grimm (Stratholme) is ATT's NPC 11058 "Fras Siabi / Ezra Grimm" (its quest The Great Ezra Grimm, 5214, names him). The NPC ids come from AllTheThings, never from this file.
sources.screenshot: The user on 2026-11-10 with a screenshot of another addon's dungeon journal: the Drowned City's bosses in the game's order (1 Zul'Alai, 3 Var'Taka, 4 Deathless Marrow, 7 Captain Dreadrise; 2 Gill, 5 Umbra and 6 Zin'aka rares, 8 cut off). Used only where AllTheThings confirms the boss (an encounter with its id); the rares and Deathless Marrow have no encounter there and stay out. Assumption (D-100): Deathless Marrow is the screenshot's name of the encounter Deathless Guardians (3478), the one encounter of ATT's list it does not show by name; Primeval Elemental and Min'loth the Serpent (not in the screenshot) follow in ATT's order.
